title: Gray–Scott: from time symmetry to looping patterns
scopeNote: User messages, assistant replies, and progress updates from September 4–5, 2026, through the request to publish this transcript. Tool logs and private runtime instructions are omitted. Automatic browser context and attachment wrappers are removed; structured question replies are formatted for reading. Local links are rewritten to public copies or the corresponding live pages. Earlier reports are preserved as written, including findings that were superseded later in the conversation.

messages.text:
Here's some context "Btw a neat application of wallpaper symmetry is differential equations. 
satisfy reaction-diffusion equations locally, while globally  it has a symmetry of a wallpaper group. You often get structures like gliders from in Conway's Game of Life
[[https://bulatov.org/symsim/240103\_JMM/index.html#(1)\](https://bulatov.org/symsim/240103\_JMM/index.html#(1\\))](https://bulatov.org/symsim/240103_JMM/index.html#\(1\)]\(https://bulatov.org/symsim/240103_JMM/index.html#\(1\\\)\))
Something that's been on my mind recently, can it be extended to time symmetry?
Looping animation where the right side of the solution is a mirror-reflected version of the left side but with a time shift. ". Specifically, I want you to take clockwork symmetry 442 which has 6 symmetries that interpret as time symmetries ([https://yaroslavvb.github.io/animated-groups-fable/correspondence-p4.html#g94](https://yaroslavvb.github.io/animated-groups-fable/correspondence-p4.html#g94)), and develop a solver that can find periodic solutions that also satisfy time symmetries. First, decide on the feasibility of finding the periodic solutions with the symmetries of the six different groups. Then create a section ("scott-gray") which focuses on 442 groups specifically, and allows me to view the animations in the browser. The original symmetric Gray-Scott are also implemented in [https://github.com/vbulatov2011/symhub/tree/main/apps/symsim/gray\_scott](https://github.com/vbulatov2011/symhub/tree/main/apps/symsim/gray_scott), I especially like the gliders attached, Prefer animations for patterns like this.

messages.text: The six groups in your correspondence are forward time symmetries, so they are compatible with autonomous Gray–Scott dynamics. A separate issue is whether a chosen parameter set produces a nonstationary orbit with the required timing; simply replaying a rotated pattern would not establish that. I’m checking the exact phase shifts and glider parameters before choosing the solver constraints.

messages.text: All six are algebraically feasible, including the two with a half-cell translation coupled to a half-period shift. There is one useful constraint: a whole 442 pattern cannot drift rigidly in a single direction. The promising targets are coordinated local gliders, rotating packets, and breathing worms. The page will let you compare those symmetry patterns, evolve the actual equations, and search for a periodic orbit with measured errors.

The underlying purpose is for this page 442: I want to be able to explore different solutions. It seems there are two directions of exploration, starting with Vladimir Bulatov's presets:  

- parameters
- images

  I want you to precompute a set of working, perfect solutions and then figure out a nice way to explore them. Perhaps only a small number of parameters are visible, and once I fix the parameters, the number of visible images is fixed.  In the original Bulatov thing, I can draw on the images. I need a different interface to explore the periodic patterns. Maybe precompute a set of parameters for which there exist images starting from initial conditions. I want to precompute a set of periodic solutions for various settings of parameters.  At the top level, I select the parameters, and for each selection, I should have a few symmetries and a few solutions that obey the given time symmetry. It's a three-way selector:  

1. The top level selects the symmetry.
2. The second one selects the parameters from a few precomputed ones that have non-zero solutions.
3. After selecting the parameters, I select one of the solutions that, in Bulatov, correspond to drawing on the plane.

  Because it's restrictive, maybe just precompute a few of them. Feel free to use an A100 model to automate the search.
